mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea local registration office (Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: certified registry extract issued by the Court Registry is a public document and is submitted directly to the Apostille Section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for a Hague Apostille. Non-member state: no apostille; the public document is submitted through the consular legalization track exclusively to the destination state's embassy or consulate in Korea, with any required MOFA authentication performed solely as part of the consular route. The two routes are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: the tax clearance certificate is an official public document and is apostilled directly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no prior notarization is required. Non-member state: do not obtain an apostille; the certificate is legalized by the destination state's consulate in Korea using the consular legalization path only. The Hague Apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or sole shareholder of the intended Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: signatures of each authorized officer or director are notarized by a Korean notary, after which the notarized instrument is submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for a Hague Apostille. Non-member state: after the same notarization, the instrument is submitted only for consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in Korea; no apostille is obtained. The two authentication paths are used in the alternative, never sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Intended Yuhan Hoesa shareholders, notarized by a licensed Korean notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: the Articles of Association must be notarized in Korea and then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Non-member state: the notarized Articles are submitted to the destination state's consular authority for legalization under the consular legalization track; an apostille must not be attached. Each destination determines which single path applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in Korea maintaining the prospective corporate account relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: the bank officer's signature on the letter is notarized by a Korean notary and the notarized letter is then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Non-member state: the notarized bank letter is legalized by the destination state's consulate in Korea using the consular legalization route solely; no Hague Apostille is requested. The two legalization families are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All prospective directors, shareholders, signatories, agents and beneficial owners of the Yuhan Hoesa must be screened before formation against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Republic of Korea's own designated persons list issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's high-risk and watch-list indicators. Politically exposed persons, including current or former foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates, trigger enhanced due diligence requiring senior management approval, written source-of-wealth documentation, source-of-funds evidence, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Automated sanctions screening must occur at onboarding, on every name or control change, and in real time for payment-rail and Shopify Payments transactions; positive hits are to be escalated to the company's AML compliance officer for freezing, reporting to KoFIU under the Specific Financial Transaction Information Act, and filing of suspicious transaction reports where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO), the official court-operated electronic registration portal for corporate name clearance, trade-name preservation registration, company incorporation filings, and certified corporate records.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Yuhan Hoesa must have a corporate name written in Hangeul including the mandatory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa.' Foreign words are transliterated phonetically into Hangeul; a secondary non-Korean name may be recorded in parentheses but cannot replace the Hangeul name. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) the company legal suffix, (2) a distinctive or arbitrary discriminating term, (3) a permissible business-purpose or descriptive element consistent with the commercial registry's purpose classifications, and (4) a Hangeul transliteration of any foreign words with no misleading similarity to existing registered names in the same or similar business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the court registration office rejects a proposed trade name on the grounds of identity or substantial similarity with an existing name, the applicant may file a written objection with the chief of the registration office that issued the rejection, attaching a search report from the IRO, a statement of the distinguishing features, and if available, prior trademark registration evidence or written consent of the existing trade-name holder. The competent court registrar must review and issue a written decision. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Litigation Case Procedure Act to the relevant district court or appellate court within fourteen calendar days of service of the refusal. The appeal should be accompanied by the statutory fee and may be delegated to a licensed Korean attorney; filing the appeal does not automatically stay the expiration of any name-reservation period, so a fresh reservation should be filed simultaneously where urgency exists.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean courts and the National Tax Service accept a virtual office or commercial mailbox for corporate registration only if it is a real domestic address where statutory notices, tax invoices, and court documents can be personally served and where the company maintains some physical indication of business activity such as work space, telephone service, or inventory records. For an online retail seller of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments, no special industry license is required, but a virtual office is frequently rejected by Korean banks during corporate account opening because Financial Intelligence Unit customer due diligence standards require verification of the actual place of business and physical control over the registered address. National Tax Service audit officers also may disallow certain VAT-deductible expenses or issue a business-suspension notice if the address is only a mail-forwarding box with no human presence. A serviced office with a dedicated address, lease agreement, utility invoice, and access-controlled workspace is recommended to reduce bank, tax, and registry friction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for possible unannounced inspection: external signage bearing the registered business name; access to the registered suite; a desk and filing facility; telecommunication or server equipment; inventory boxes or shipping records; utility and rent receipts; and an identifiable representative or employee. The National Tax Service uses sampling-based field verification for newly registered e-commerce sellers, and local municipal authorities may check registration tax details. Quantified risk: approximately 10-15% estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site visit within the first 18 months for a dedicated serviced office, rising to 35-50% for a virtual-office or shared mailing address; postal verification and telephone confirmation risk approaches 100% for any newly formed Yuhan Hoesa during the initial VAT registration and compliance-review period.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act, as amended; the Limited Liability Company chapter (Articles 543–613) governs Yuhan Hoesa; sections 544, 550, 553, 563, and 580; together with the Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Rules, and the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce for online retail operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company; online filings are submitted through the Supreme Court of Korea Court Registry Information System (IROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), together with the executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The paid-in capital amount is fixed in the Articles of Incorporation, and all contributions must be fully paid and deposited into a domestic bank account opened in the prospective corporate name before the registration application is submitted. The bank's certificate of paid-in capital or certificate of deposit must be filed with the registration court. No blocked escrow account is mandated by statute; the funds remain as the Company's capital after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
THIS FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS of KR_YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, is adopted by unanimous written consent of all directors on the date indicated in the corporate record. The directors have reviewed the Articles of Incorporation, the capital subscription evidence, the bank certificate of paid-in capital, and the proposed registered office address, and the following resolutions are adopted.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. RESOLVED, that the initial capital of the Company is fixed at the amount set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into the number of membership units set forth therein, and that all such membership units have been validly subscribed by the founding members and fully paid in cash into the provisional subscription account opened in the name of the Company at a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea. The directors accept the bank certificate of paid-in capital as conclusive evidence of full payment. The Representative Director is directed to preserve the certificate and attach the same to the incorporation registration dossier.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company is hereby adopted as the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, within the jurisdiction of the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having competence over such address, and that all legal notices, service of process and official communications shall be delivered to such address. The Representative Director is authorized and directed to file the incorporation registration within two weeks from the date of notarial execution of the Articles of Incorporation and to cause the registered office to be publicly disclosed.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the commercial bank designated in the Articles of Incorporation and the corporate account opened for capital subscription are approved as the principal banking and treasury relationship of the Company. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, are hereby authorized to open, maintain, operate and close bank accounts, execute electronic funds transfer instructions, accept payments through Stripe and Shopify Payments, and execute all banking, treasury, loan, and guarantee documents on behalf of the Company.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the individuals identified in the officers schedule are appointed as the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, Director and Chief Financial Officer, and any other directors identified in the schedule, each to hold office until the first annual general meeting of members. The directors further resolve that no statutory auditor is required under the Korean Commercial Act and the External Audit Act because the paid-in capital is below the statutory audit threshold, and accordingly no auditor is appointed. Each officer is authorized to execute under the corporate seal, engage legal and tax advisers, and take all lawful actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Name Search System (IROS) and the Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability check for the proposed company name through the Supreme Court of Korea commercial registration name search portal. The proposed name must include Yuhan Hoesa or another permitted corporate identifier and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. After identifying two or three acceptable names, draft the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act; the articles must include the company name, the corporate purpose covering online retail of desktop 3D printers, resin filaments and consumables, the registered office address, the amount of capital, the number of membership units and their contribution amounts, the names of each founding member, the term, the number of directors and the representation method. Review the draft with corporate counsel and tax counsel to verify that the business purpose is ISIC 4791 and that no industrial license is required. Complete the corporate seal declaration and prepare the notary and registration folders.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft
Name search results or confirmation of name availability
Passport or resident registration certificate copies of each founding member
Notarized power of attorney for each attorney-in-fact, if applicable
Corporate seal declaration and seal imprint certificate
Corporate purpose description in English (ISIC 4791)
Consent to incorporation draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns an identical or confusingly similar mark, choose one of the backup names and amend the draft articles before notarization. If the court queries the purpose clause, narrow the wording to online retail sale via the internet of desktop 3D printers, resin filaments and consumables and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Provisional Capital Subscription Account and Deposit of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Banking Department of a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, including banks authorized to issue certificates of paid-in capital for commercial registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital subscription account with a licensed Korean commercial bank in the name of the proposed company, using the corporate seal or signature cards of the founding members. Each founding member must wire or deposit the amount of his or her subscribed contribution into this account. After all contributions are received, request the bank to issue an official certificate of payment of capital or certificate of deposit specifying the account name, account number, amount, date, and identity of the depositors. This certificate is a mandatory document for the incorporation registration. The bank account will become the Company's first corporate operating account upon registration, but the representative director should request that the bank annotate the account with the corporate registration number after the court completes the registration process. No blocked escrow arrangement is required under Korean law.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Founding members' identification documents
Bank account application and signature card for the provisional account
AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declaration
Certificate of deposit or certificate of paid-in capital issued by the bank
Corporate seal temporary imprint, if provided
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC or source-of-funds documentation, provide certified passport copies, bank account statements, and a completed source of funds declaration. If the certificate contains any discrepancy, request immediate correction; no registration filing may proceed until the corrected certificate is delivered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public under Korean notary law, or the notarial office attached to the local District Court; for foreign-language documents, a certified translation may additionally be notarized.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange for the execution of the Articles of Incorporation before a notary authorized under Korean notary law. All incorporators, or their attorneys-in-fact, must appear in person, verify their identities, and affix their signatures or corporate seals. The notary will confirm that the articles are legal, that the founders have voluntarily consented, and that the corporate purpose is lawful and definite. For any incorporator acting through an attorney, the notary requires a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. After execution, the notary will certify the Articles of Incorporation. The notarized original, together with the capital payment certificate and the minutes or consent of incorporation, forms the core of the registration dossier. Avoid any alteration after notarization unless the amendment is initialed by all parties and re-certified by the notary.
required_dossiers: Original draft Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital from the bank
Identity documents or seal certificates of all incorporators
Notarized power of attorney and apostille or consular legalization, if applicable
Minutes or written consent of incorporation
Corporate registration number reservation record, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to certify because of a defective purpose clause or incomplete signature, cure the articles by executing an amendment signed by all founders; if a power of attorney lacks legalization, obtain apostille and resubmit. The notarial certificate date must be restated after re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the Commercial Registration Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Court Registry Information System (IROS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation registration application to the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office. The application may also be filed online through the court's e-Registration system. Include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of paid-in capital, the corporate seal certificate, the minutes of incorporation, the appointment documentation of the representative director and other statutory officers, and proof of the registered office address. Pay the registration tax, education surtax and court filing fee at the court's treasury counter or e-payment portal. The registration must be completed within two weeks after the notarial execution of the Articles of Incorporation. Upon successful review, the court assigns a corporate registration number and issues a certificate of incorporation registration evidencing the legal existence of the Company.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation in the form prescribed by the Supreme Court
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital from the bank
Minutes or consent of incorporation
Consent of directors and officers and their seal certificates
Proof of registered office address, such as a lease agreement or owner consent
Corporate seal registration certificate
Receipt of payment of registration tax and court fees
Application for taxpayer corporate registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a request for correction, attend to the stated defects within the court-prescribed period, usually one to two weeks; provide the missing notarized original or corrected bank certificate. If the court rejects the filing, submit a written objection or motion for re-examination under the Commercial Registration Act; appeal remains available for legal error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and E-Commerce Operator Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, and the local municipal consumer-protection unit responsible for electronic commerce notifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation registration certificate is issued, apply to the National Tax Service for Corporate Tax and Value-Added Tax registration and obtain the business registration certificate for the Company. Provide the company name, registration number, address, representatives, business purpose classified as ISIC 4791, bank account details, and e-mail contact. Since the Company is an online retail seller, also register a consumer-protection identifier under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce where the company posts its business identity in its online shopfront, including the Stripe and Shopify Payments checkout pages. If the Company will hire employees, register with the four major social security systems within the statutory deadlines. These post-incorporation tax and consumer-compliance filings are distinct from industrial licensing and are mandatory before sales commence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporation registration
Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Proof of registered office address, such as lease contract or ownership certificate
Resident representative officer identification
Bank statement or certificate of capital payment
Corporate contact information and e-mail address
Application form for business registration certificate
Application for electronic commerce operator notification, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends issuance of the business registration certificate because the business purpose appears to cover manufacturing, submit a confirmatory letter and amended tax-purpose description stating that the company will sell products manufactured by third parties and will not operate a factory; furnish the lease contract or office rental certificate and reapply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. This enterprise is ISIC 4791, retail sale via mail order or the internet, and does not fall within the industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing categories (ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx). No industrial licensing board or municipal industrial licensing agency is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating permit is required for the online retail of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments. The only mandatory registration is the National Tax Service business registration certificate, which is a tax registration rather than an industrial license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea does not require an Environmental Impact Assessment for pure online retail operations under ISIC 4791.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. The operation is categorized as e-commerce retail sales and is not listed among activities subject to full EIA, preliminary EIA, or environmental registration because there is no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or industrial facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The Company does not own or operate a manufacturing plant and therefore has no wastewater discharge, VOC emission, or hazardous waste generation points. The Company will comply with ordinary municipal solid waste disposal rules for office packaging and returned goods and will not store chemicals, resins, or materials in quantities that trigger hazardous materials permitting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No Civil Defense fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required because the Company does not operate a factory, chemical facility, warehouse, or other installation subject to the Fire Services Act or the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The Company will follow general office occupancy safety and fire prevention practices for its administrative office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr. Export/customs interface: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa LLC: submit the Business Registration Application to the NTS through HomeTax or the district tax office within 20 days of business commencement, attaching the certified Registrar Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, domestic place-of-business lease or ownership evidence, and representative/shareholder identity documents. The NTS then issues the Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business, the entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and apply to the NTS/HomeTax for a non-resident Foreign Business Registration Number (BRN) before making taxable supplies; a KCS bonded/import-export registration is additionally required for physical cross-border goods transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea has no check-the-box or elective hybrid-mismatch pass-through. The Yuhan Hoesa LLC is mandatorily a separate Korean resident taxable corporation under the Corporate Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 / no general registration threshold for domestic suppliers; VAT registration is compulsory from business commencement for any person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea. A simplified taxpayer regime may reduce compliance burden for small domestic merchants, but VAT registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issuance through NTS HomeTax e-Bill/e-Invoice interfaces for every VAT-registered business. Invoices must be issued to all VAT-registered customers no later than the day following the supply and transmitted digitally to the NTS via certified ERP/API integration where applicable. Korea does not employ real-time pre-clearance fiscal stamping; the NTS instead performs automated cross-matching of e-tax invoice data against VAT returns and customs records for post-filing anti-fraud control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of goods are zero-rated under Article 24 of the VAT Act when the goods physically depart Korea as evidenced by an accepted KCS export declaration, the purchaser is a foreign person/entity, and export proceeds are received in foreign currency and repatriated/settled in accordance with Korean foreign-exchange rules. For online retail of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments/consumables, export-by-parcel clearance must be made through UNI-PASS with confirmed foreign delivery; qualifying exported B2B services are also zero-rated, but the present scope is physical goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / export parcel consignment evidence
Export Sales Contract or Purchase Order
Foreign Exchange Purchase and Settlement Certificate / bank remittance advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Proof of actual physical export including KCS customs examination report and carrier departure proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that export documents are false, goods did not actually leave Korea, or the foreign-currency proceeds were not received within the 180-day repatriation deadline (or an approved extension), the zero-rating is denied: 10% VAT is assessed on the full export value plus statutory additional tax under the VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes (including civil penalties of up to 40% for fraudulent evasion and 20% for negligent underreporting), late-payment interest, and potential criminal liability for tax evasion; the exporter may additionally lose UNI-PASS fast clearance and export-zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), as the central bank and foreign exchange authority, acting together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the electronic financial supervision framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalised but regulated foreign exchange regime rather than a strict capital-control system. The Bank of Korea, through authorised foreign exchange banks, requires declarations/reports for significant cross-border transactions, but does not routinely approve every remittance. The Korean won (KRW) is convertible on current account: export/import payments, royalties, service fees, and dividends may be settled freely if supporting documentation is retained. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment, loans, and sureties, are reportable and need a genuine economic purpose. Export proceeds are not forcibly surrendered; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign exchange accounts. However, profit remittance and dividend payments require the bank to hold audited financial statements, tax payment confirmation, withholding tax certificate, and a valid foreign investment report to prove access to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) benefit. In practice, banks enforce local substance checks, customer due diligence, and BOK reporting, making onboarding dependent on clean documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export receipts must be received within six months (or such extended period as approved by the Bank of Korea) after the export declaration date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won; the full export proceeds may be retained in a domestic foreign currency account, but the receipt must be reported to the licensed foreign exchange bank and preserved as evidence of export performance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs domiciled outside Korea are not licensed under the Korean Banking Act or Electronic Financial Transactions Act and cannot serve as the principal clearing bank for a Yuhan Hoesa. They cannot provide a domestic KRW account for tax payments, VAT, payroll, or local commercial settlements. A registered domestic specialised electronic financial business may provide foreign exchange payment services only with a licensed bank settlement account. Therefore, cross-border EMIs are legally barred as primary treasury rails and should be used solely as payment-acquiring aggregators (Stripe, Shopify Payments). Viability rating: Low for a corporate bank account; Medium as a payments aggregation layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is effectively mandatory for corporate account onboarding. Korean banks require at least one statutory director and all authorised signatories to attend the account-opening meeting in a Korean branch with an original passport or Alien Registration Card, the corporate seal, apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, and board resolution. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted under Korean real-name verification and AML obligations. A non-resident director may appoint a local Korean-resident financial manager under a notarised power of attorney, but the initial KYC interview remains in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online e-commerce founder selling 3D printers and resin filaments maintains high cross-border counterparty velocity, including early-stage prepayments from unrelated jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contract inventory showing purchase orders and sales invoices, shipping bills of lading, freight/customs declarations, Stripe/Shopify settlement statements, full UBO registry with photo IDs and proof of business address for all shareholders, and source-of-funds bank statements from each material remitting company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection into the Korean LLC is not matched by a registered foreign investment certificate, creating unauthorised capital-account entry suspicion under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment report confirmation issued by the domestic bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, passport/Tax Identification Number of foreign investor, certificate of incorporation, articles of association, board resolution approving share issuance, share subscription agreement, inward remittance advice with FDI purpose code, Certificate of Foreign Investment, and bank/CPA capital verification report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Resin and filament products may present dual-use or export-control ambiguity, triggering an enterprise-wide sanctions/diversion review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product Safety Data Sheets, harmonized system classification, ECCN determination from a licensed customs broker, end-user/end-use certificates from commercial purchasers, restricted-party screening results across UN/EU/US/Korea lists, geo-blocking and screening policy documentation, and a clean export-compliance deployment protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound remittance denominations and values are inconsistent with the stated turnover of an early-stage LLC, triggering high-value unusual transaction reporting to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with financial projections, platform settlement records, underlying customer invoices, electronic tax invoices, investor capital deposit minutes, source-of-wealth certificates for shareholders, and written explanations for each material foreign remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward foreign direct investment must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's corporate account to the LLC's domestic foreign-currency account at a Tier-1 Korean bank. The remittance must carry a genuine purpose code for equity acquisition or foreign direct investment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the bank files the foreign-exchange declaration and the investor reports under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the investment is reportable. After registration, the bank issues a Certificate of Foreign Investment. The foreign currency is converted to KRW at the market rate, and capital verification is performed by the bank or CPA. For e-commerce receivables, export card settlements from Stripe/Shopify are reported as current-account receipt through the online payment provider and swept into the operating account at the local bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-related payments for 3D-print resins, spare parts, filaments, and freight are executed through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account purchases; irrevocable commercial letters of credit for high-value or first-time supplier purchases; and documentary collections (D/P or D/A) when the bank needs to hold title documents until payment or acceptance. Export trade settlement can be under T/T open account for repeat buyers, and the local bank handles BOK declarative reporting. For e-commerce outbound customer refunds, the Stripe/Shopify settlement engine must reconcile with the bank account through a controlled payment account, and cards/trade refunds must be paired with the original transaction ID to avoid suspicious mismatches.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign-exchange contracts permitted only against documented current or capital account exposure, typically up to the underlying trade amount, with maturity matched to the settlement date of the underlying Korean export/import contract.

Korean-won non-deliverable forwards executable only through licensed FX market participants for non-resident or offshore underlying positions, with actual trade exposure documentation; speculative NDFs are restricted.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps available only for hedging foreign-currency debt or material investment cash-flow mismatches, requiring board-approval minutes, bank ISDA or Korean FX master agreement, valuation marks, and BOK post-trade reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return and Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - District Tax Office via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, file on or before March 31 of the following year (within 3 months after fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of unpaid tax; understatement surcharge of 10%; daily late-payment interest at 0.022% per day on unpaid tax; continued non-payment permits NTS compulsory collection through asset seizure. The Korean commercial register does not administratively strike off this entity for tax delinquency; strike-off only occurs through judicial liquidation/deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim Corporate Income Tax Return (Interim Prepayment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - District Tax Office via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa with interim period January 1 through June 30, file and pay on or before August 31 of the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay interim corporate tax triggers the same national-tax surcharges: 20% non-filing surcharge, 10% understatement surcharge, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; no administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax (Local Surtax) Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government of the place of business (Si/Gun/Gu) through the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, file and pay on or before March 31 of the following year, in parallel with the national corporate tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local Tax Act imposes 20% non-filing surcharge, 10% understatement surcharge, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; local authorities may carry out compulsory collection through seizure and sale of property. This is not a registry strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax (Local Surtax) Interim Prepayment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government of the place of business (Si/Gun/Gu) through the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year entity, the interim local corporate tax prepayment is due on or before August 31 of the same year for the period January 1 through June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers 20% non-filing surcharge, 10% understatement surcharge, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; local authorities may seek compulsory seizure. No administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Return - First Half Preliminary Period (January 1 to March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - District Tax Office via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay on or before April 25 of the same calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing or underpayment triggers a 20% additional tax on unpaid VAT, a 10% understatement additional tax, and daily late-payment interest at 0.022%; continued default may lead to business-site closure and asset seizure. No automatic registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies, an independent CPA audit is mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa LLC if any of the following triggers are met: (1) balance-sheet trigger: total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.7 million); (2) public-interest trigger: the company is listed on a Korean stock exchange or is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission; (3) special-order trigger: a court, regulator, financial institution, or shareholder-protection process requires an external audit. Korean law does not impose a general turnover or employee-count statutory audit threshold for an unlisted Yuhan Hoesa LLC; the balance-sheet asset threshold is the principal quantitative criterion.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and those required to adopt IFRS; otherwise Korea Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) and the Korean SME Accounting Standards for small enterprises. Financial statements are prepared under the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on External Audit of Companies, and tax book income is reconciled to taxable income under the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require an annual centralized UBO return for a Yuhan Hoesa LLC. The statutory protocol is event-driven: any share transfer, change in foreign ownership percentage, capital change, director change, or registered-office change must be reported to the relevant authority (KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for foreign-invested enterprises) within 30 days of the triggering event. Practically, the company should conduct an annual ownership and control confirmation at the annual shareholder/partner meeting, update its statutory registers, and verify that the court registry and tax office records reflect the current UBOs, directors, and members.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax, plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined top headline rate of 26.4% for taxable income above KRW 300 billion; progressive lower brackets are 9%, 19%, and 21%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box regime for 3D printer hardware e-commerce; statutory incentives include an R&D tax credit for qualifying R&D expenses, free economic zone and foreign investment zone tax holidays with up to 50-100% corporate tax exemptions for a limited period, and certain SME tax benefits, but pure online retail distribution is ordinarily outside the preferential tax holiday regimes
